examples.label: Enumerate inside MySQL

notes: Default port 3306. Try root/blank and root/root. `SHOW databases;` then hunt creds in app schemas. FILE privilege enables LOAD_FILE reads and INTO OUTFILE webshell writes.

recommended.note: Read files / write a webshell via FILE priv.

name: MySQL - Enumeration
description: Scan MySQL with NSE, then log in (empty or discovered password) and enumerate databases/tables/versions.

defense.why_it_works: Adversaries scan for open ports and running services on network hosts to identify attack surface and potential exploitation targets. Tools like netcat, nmap, and service-specific clients probe for banner information that reveals software versions, which can then be matched against known vulnerabilities.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to MySQL (TCP 3306); credentials for authenticated queries.
defense.impact: Server version, databases, and users; with credentials, data access and possible file read/write.
defense.detection: Monitor for processes performing network enumeration by correlating process creation, socket connections, and sequential destination IP probing within a time window. Unusual port scanning patterns or banner-grabbing activity from internal hosts can indicate post-compromise discovery.
defense.artifacts: Connection and authentication attempts in MySQL logs; traffic to 3306.
defense.prevention: Close unnecessary ports and services to prevent risk of discovery and potential exploitation. Use network intrusion detection/prevention systems to detect and prevent remote service scans. Ensure proper network segmentation to protect critical servers and devices.
defense.misconfiguration: The application constructs SQL queries using string concatenation with unsanitized user input — either in the query body or stored procedure arguments. No prepared statements or parameterized queries are used. Additionally, the database user account used by the application has excessive privileges (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on all tables, or even xp_cmdshell access on MSSQL).
defense.evasion: Re-disable any risky setting after use; read files via SQL directly; avoid writing webshells where a read suffices.
